alt: Poster: SEBI revises closing auction and expiry settlement - 30-minute VWAP settlement, auction 3:30-3:40 pm, most changes effective 7 Dec 2026
text:
SEBI has revised how expiring derivatives will be settled, and the market is discussing it.

• SEBI announced on 15 October that expiring index and stock derivatives will settle on the VWAP of the last 30 minutes of continuous trading (3:00 to 3:30 pm), replacing the earlier closing-auction-based price, per Business Standard and Upstox (PTI).
• The Closing Auction Session will run as a separate 10-minute session from 3:30 to 3:40 pm, with the cash-segment post-close session from 3:50 to 4:00 pm, per Upstox (PTI) and Goodreturns.
• Most changes take effect on 7 December 2026; rules for moving unexecuted limit and iceberg orders into the auction take effect on 8 February 2027, per Business Standard.
• The auction was introduced on 3 August; Business Standard reports it drew complaints about settlement prices, sharp spikes and low liquidity.

Our view: separating expiry settlement from the closing auction may reduce the chance that a thin auction moves settlement values, though how it works in practice will only be visible after the new rules go live. Participants may also need to revisit how they plan around expiry-day timings. This is an interpretation, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: how do you expect a last-30-minute VWAP settlement to change the way you manage positions around expiry?
